status: Retained-world bundles hold only referenced streams and expose prepared allocation-to-pane associations
production_consumers: Default board and schematic retained-world bundle preparation and reuse
retired_paths: Unconditional retention and cache invalidation on unused vertex/stroke buffers
behavior: Bundle keys and lifetime holds now include only world streams referenced by their encoded draw batches. Replacing an unused stream preserves the cached bundle.

Each cached bundle records current pane/surface metadata. An allocation-free renderer iterator exposes its allocation IDs, including the bound pane uniform. Pane identity changes update metadata without rebuilding unchanged GPU commands.
Shared world allocation IDs appear for each referencing pane; process byte accounting remains one record per allocation. SubmissionRef retains its existing GPU lifetime hold.

proof.renderer: 384 tests passed in the broad renderer run; the sole failure was the new fixture assuming only one preexisting surface. After explicitly selecting one source pane before adding a second, the affected actual-GPU test passed. Its earlier failure from reusing hidden quad commands is also preserved. No production-code changes followed the broad run.
proof.checks: Strict renderer/app visual all-target Clippy, fresh offline GUI build, source health and governance checks pass.

limits: This iterator reports prepared cached-world associations, not submitted/presented pane usage. Shell, overlay, text and terminal logical-consumer association remains unfinished; no all-consumer adoption or predicate closure.
All seven recorded S4 implementation gaps and original S5 qualification remain. No dependency, vendor, license, prototype, numerical-cap or sequencing change; preserve GEFN and nonblocking resize.
